clue.text: Girl's discs are not in order

definitions.note: the possessive here reads as 'girl is', the definition being the girl

indicators.note: letters not in their proper order have been jumbled, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's record collection has been shelved haphazardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl's' is 'Girl is', with the definition a heroine's name; 'not in order' rearranges the letters of DISCS ARE. Cressida is the faithless heroine of Troilus and Cressida.
explanation.definitionFit: Cressida is a female first name, best known from Shakespeare's Trojan heroine.

indicators.note: off here means taken away, so one piece is removed from the other

parts.note: smallest means least
L stands for learner, a pupil driver, from the L-plate

explanation.surface: A school compass reading taken after the littlest child has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes L, the learner (from the British L-plate on a learner driver's car), from LEAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass bearing can be one of the cardinal points, the direction of sunrise.

clue.text: Key into source, turning up a problem

indicators.note: into here means one piece goes inside the other
in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a mine is a source, as in a mine of information
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: Putting a key into a lock and discovering something goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts G inside MINE to make MGINE; with A in front that is AMGINE, and 'turning up' reads it upwards in this down clue. The 'a' looks like part of 'a problem' but is a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a puzzle or mystery, something baffling to solve.
As slang the word means excellent; as a noun it means calm composure under pressure.

clue.text: Be specific about period object on sale

parts.note: a spell is a period of time
it is a pronoun for an object
a book that is out has been published and is on sale

explanation.surface: An antique dealer describes a piece from a certain era being offered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' is the pronoun IT, not a thing; 'period' looks like an antique's era but is SPELL.
explanation.definitionFit: To state something plainly and in full detail leaves no room for doubt.

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
to hang is to project or jut out, as in an overhang; the 's is 'is', a link

explanation.surface: A musical note describes how a project has been revived.
explanation.definitionFit: Pictures or curtains taken down and hung once more have been rehung.

parts.note: a trial is a court hearing
to run is to function, as a machine does

explanation.surface: An audiologist checks how well someone's ears work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' suggests ears but is a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal or practice exercise checks that something works before real use.

parts.note: re is a note of the sol-fa scale
port is the left side of a ship
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A memo about leaving time for a factual film.
explanation.definitionFit: Reportage is factual journalistic coverage, the kind of material a documentary presents.

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
game animals are hunted as prey

explanation.surface: A huge pheasant or grouse for the shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game bird' reads as one phrase, but 'game' is PREY and 'bird' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a fish-eating raptor, a large bird of prey.

parts.note: concrete that is set has gone hard
someone standing is up on their feet

explanation.surface: Hard standing, a paved parking area, made by some arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard standing' is a British term for a paved area for vehicles; split, the words give SET and UP.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-up is the way something is organised or laid out.

clue.text: A dog fell scrambling over sheet metal

indicators.note: scrambling means mixing up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog tumbles while clambering over a sheet of corrugated metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambling' rearranges A DOG FELL; 'over' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold beaten into extremely thin sheets is used for gilding.

parts.note: not computer pictures: images made with the digits, the fingers, as children do with paint

explanation.definitionFit: Children dab paint with their fingers to make pictures, so the art is literally made by digits.

clue.text: Check stuff about wrong location in Kent

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: gingham is a checked cotton fabric, stuff being cloth
ill means wrong or bad, as in ill-gotten

explanation.surface: Inspecting material for errors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' looks like a verb but describes the pattern of the cloth; 'about' puts GINGHAM around ILL. Gillingham is a town in Kent, a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Gillingham is a town on the Medway, part of the Kent county area.

clue.text: Fruit variety aren't nice when cooked

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are altered or doctored, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some fruit tastes unpleasant once it has been cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges the letters of AREN'T NICE (the apostrophe is ignored); 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-skinned kind of peach, it is a cultivated variety of that fruit.

parts.note: to float a company is to launch it on the stock market

explanation.surface: A ship is about to be launched into the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to launch' reads as a ship's moment, but splits into A and FLOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat on the water is floating, so being at sea means being buoyant.

clue.text: Boldly confront a charge in speech

indicators.note: in speech means the words are as they sound when spoken

parts.note: a cost is a charge, a price asked

explanation.surface: Someone rudely challenges a fee they have been asked to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: Said out loud, A COST, a charge, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to approach and address them aggressively.

clue.text: Artist holds nothing against money value of sales

indicators.note: holds here means contains, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: J. M. W. Turner was the English painter
O looks like zero, nothing
V for versus means against

explanation.surface: A painter who refuses to sell makes nothing from his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts O and V inside TURNER, the English landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's turnover is the total income it takes in from trading.

clue.text: Learn since then about garden plant

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener has learned about a plant since some time ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges LEARN SINCE THEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Physalis, whose papery orange seed cases look like paper lamps, is grown in gardens.

clue.text: Appeal to do without the lot

indicators.note: without here means outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle or con them
the lot means all, everything

explanation.surface: Asking someone to manage without everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense outside: CON goes around ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask someone formally for help or action is to make a request of them.

clue.text: Use money invested in energy scheme

indicators.note: invested in here means placed inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
a ploy is a scheme or tactic
M is short for money in financial notation, as in M1 for money supply

explanation.surface: Putting cash into an energy project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in' puts M between E and PLOY.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ a method or tool is to put it to work.

indicators.note: stuck on here means attached in front, one piece placed before the other

parts.note: to flag something is to label or tag it
hip means fashionable, stylish

explanation.surface: Price tags stuck on a fashionable shopping bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrier' suggests a carrier bag but is the naval sense: a fleet's leading vessel, often an aircraft carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleet's lead vessel carrying the admiral is often an aircraft carrier in modern navies.

indicators.note: has left means is gone, so one piece is removed from the other

parts.note: a jar is a jolt or shock

explanation.surface: A jar of wine, and the son has gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jar' looks like a container but is a jolt; 'has left' removes S. Hock is the British name for German white wine from the Rhine.
explanation.definitionFit: Hock is a white wine from the Rhineland of Germany.

indicators.note: of here means the answer is made of letters running inside the words

explanation.surface: Asking whether Florida is a hot state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like part of 'State of Florida' but stands alone; the answer runs across FloridA HOt.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the United States, in the north-west.

indicators.note: we hear means the word sounds like another when spoken

parts.note: to weigh with someone is to influence them

explanation.surface: Gossip that some American influence has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: WEIGH, influence, said out loud gives WAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not present is absent, gone elsewhere.

parts.note: not paid labour by the item: a work of art built of many small pieces of tile or glass

explanation.definitionFit: A picture assembled from small tiles or stones is literally a work made of pieces.

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to orate is to make a public speech
PE is physical education, training at school

explanation.surface: Someone gave a speech about running training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' is the definition, in its sense of managed, not a jog; 'about' puts ORATED around PE.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a machine or business is to work it, make it function.
